$description: Tajeer AI's MOBILE design language. This file is the single source of truth for every colour, type step, spacing step, radius, elevation and motion value in the Flutter client, and `tool/build_tokens.dart` generates `lib/app/theme/tokens.g.dart` from it. It is deliberately NOT packages/tajeerai-design-system/tokens.json: mobile and web are two design systems that share a brand, not one system with two renderers. It carries two PRESETS -- `aurora`, the original indigo, and `tajeer`, the warm yellow the reference design describes -- each with an intentionally designed light and dark palette. One component set renders under all four, because every preset answers to the same semantic names. Colours are authored as #RRGGBB, or as #AARRGGBB where an alpha is meant -- ALPHA FIRST, which is Dart's Color(0xAARRGGBB) order and NOT the CSS #RRGGBBAA order. There is no web consumer of this file, so it speaks Flutter.

preset.$description: The visual presets. A preset is a complete pair of palettes -- light and dark -- and the elevation that goes with them; everything else (type, spacing, radii, motion, channel identity) is shared, because a second spacing scale is a second design system. Components never name a preset: they read the semantic token, and the preset decides what it is. Adding one is adding a block here, and the generator emits it.

aurora.$description: The original palette, indigo and violet on neutral grey, carried over from the web design system this client was first transcribed from. Kept as a selectable preset so the change of identity is a choice rather than a deletion. Re-expressed in the shared semantic vocabulary -- `card` became `surface`, `foreground` became `textPrimary`, `destructive` became `dangerDefault` -- because one component set can only render under two presets if both answer to the same names. Fifteen `chart*` and `sidebar*` tokens were dropped: no line of mobile code has ever read one. Nine values moved to clear the contrast floors the shared contract imposes and the original was never held to; each says so below, and each keeps its hue.

textMuted.$description: Darkened from #6C7078. The shared component contract holds muted text to a body-text floor against every surface including the semantic washes, and the original fell to 4.28:1 on the danger wash.

successDefault.$description: Darkened from #00AA6F, which carried white ink at 3.01:1. The hue is unchanged; only the step moved.

warningDefault.$description: Darkened from #EBAA2D, which carried white ink at 2.03:1 -- an amber cannot be a solid fill under white text at any saturation. Same finding as the Tajeer preset reached independently.

infoDefault.$description: Darkened from #06B6D4 (2.43:1 with white ink). Cyan has the same problem amber does.

textMuted.$description: Lightened from #919293, which fell to 3.87:1 on the muted surface.

focus.$description: The old #6366F1 primary, kept here where it has no ink on it and its 5.31:1 against the surface makes it the better ring.

primary.$description: Was #6366F1, which carried white ink at 4.47:1 -- three hundredths under the floor. Stepped to indigo-600, where it is 5.60:1.

primaryHover.$description: Was #818CF8. Indigo-400 under white ink is 2.98:1, so in this preset hover steps toward the saturated end rather than the light one.

tajeer.$description: The Tajeer identity: a warm yellow accent on a warm-neutral day surface and a deep-navy night one. The default preset, and the one the reference design describes.

background.$description: The page canvas. Warm off-white, biased toward the brand's own hue at very low saturation rather than toward the orange-grey stone family -- so light mode reads as the yellow's own neutral instead of a second, unrelated temperature. The ink ramp stays navy, which is the joint that keeps day and night one product.

surface.$description: The primary raised surface: a card, a sheet, a list. In light mode depth is a shadow, so this stays white at every elevation level.

surfaceMuted.$description: A recess, not a raise -- an input well, a code block, a quiet row. Darker than its parent surface in BOTH themes; that consistency is what stops an inverted palette turning every input into a raised block.

surfaceElevated.$description: Menus, popovers, dialogs. Identical to surface here on purpose: see elevation.light, where the level is carried by the shadow.

surfaceOverlay.$description: The modal scrim: 60% of the dark background. Navy rather than black, so what shows through the scrim belongs to the same palette.

textPrimary.$description: Body and heading ink. The same navy as the dark theme's background -- the two themes share an ink family and an accent, and differ only in surface temperature. Worst measured case 15.35:1 on surfaceMuted.

textSecondary.$description: Supporting text that is still text. Worst case 8.92:1.

textMuted.$description: Timestamps, captions, placeholder. Tuned to clear 4.5:1 against every surface in this theme including the semantic washes -- it carries real prose, so it is held to a body-text floor rather than a large-text one.

textDisabled.$description: A control that cannot be operated. Deliberately below 4.5:1: WCAG 1.4.3 excludes disabled controls, and lifting it here would make disabled indistinguishable from enabled, which is the actual accessibility failure. contrast_test.dart exempts it by name and states this reason.

textInverse.$description: Ink ON a saturated semantic fill. Every {semantic}.default is tuned so this clears 4.5:1 on it, which is what makes one rule work instead of a per-hue table.

border.$description: The default hairline. Warm-cast rather than neutral grey, so a panel edge reads as part of this palette instead of a grey box drawn over it.

borderSubtle.$description: The quieter line: a separator inside a surface, where a full border would cut the panel in two.

borderStrong.$description: A boundary that has to be found rather than merely present -- a segmented control's edge, a table rule.

focus.$description: The focus ring, and the ONLY legal way to colour text with the brand in light mode: #FACC15 on white is 1.53:1, so the brand is a fill here and never a foreground. 4.67:1 on background.

primary.$description: The Tajeer AI accent. A fill: a primary button, a selected tab's indicator, an unread dot. Never text on a light surface.

primaryHover.$description: Hover is more energy, and energy runs toward the far end of the ramp -- which is DARKER in light mode and lighter in dark.

primaryPressed.$description: The pressed step. primaryForeground still clears 6.04:1 on it.

primarySoft.$description: The brand wash: a selected row, a soft badge, the outgoing message bubble.

primaryForeground.$description: Ink on the brand. IDENTICAL in both themes, because the yellow does not flip: 11.58:1. This is 'yellow cannot carry white text' held as one global rule rather than re-derived per theme.

primaryBorder.$description: A boundary for the yellow fill, which has none of its own: #FACC15 is 1.53:1 on white. This one token replaces the deleted opaqueBorderFor() derivation, whose fixed -8 HSL-lightness step produced 8.69:1 on the old indigo and 1.94:1 on this yellow. A lightness delta is not a contrast guarantee.

overlayHover.$description: The hover wash a Pressable paints OVER its child, whatever colour that child is. 4% black. This is why one pressable works on a card, on primarySoft and on a yellow fill without knowing which it is on.

successDefault.$description: The saturated fill. NOT the #22C55E anchor, which is 3.30:1 as a fill on white and unusable in light mode -- that anchor survives verbatim as the dark value, which is the theme it was picked against. textInverse on this: 4.76:1.

successSoft.$description: The wash behind a success badge or banner.

successForeground.$description: Ink on successSoft -- never on successDefault, which takes textInverse. 8.30:1.

successBorder.$description: A decorative hairline AROUND successSoft. Contract is visibility, not contrast, and it is never a control boundary: an error input's border uses dangerDefault, not dangerBorder.

warningDefault.$description: Orange, not amber, and this is the one place the palette departs from the brief's implied colour. With a yellow brand an amber warning IS the brand: #D97706 beside #FACC15 reads as two shades of one thing, and a status colour that can be mistaken for a resting accent is a broken status colour. 4.92:1 with textInverse.

dangerDefault.$description: Also the boundary of a control in an error state -- 6.14:1 with textInverse and 5.90:1 against the page. dangerBorder cannot do that job: it is 1.5:1 on its own wash.

infoDefault.$description: 6.36:1 with textInverse. Distinct from the channel palette's blue, which is a channel identity rather than a status.

background.$description: The canvas. Deep navy, never pure black: black gives a border or a raised surface nothing to separate from, so every panel edge would have to be drawn with a shadow instead of a tone.

surface.$description: The resting surface. One tone above the canvas -- here depth is a surface step plus a hairline, not a drop shadow, because a soft shadow on #111827 is invisible.

surfaceMuted.$description: A recess: DARKER than surface, exactly as in light mode. An inversion would have made it lighter than its parent, which is how an input well becomes a raised block.

surfaceOverlay.$description: The modal scrim: 70% of a near-black navy.

textPrimary.$description: Worst measured case 10.35:1, on the modal tone.

textMuted.$description: A deliberate departure from Tailwind gray-400 (#9CA3AF), which falls to 4.26:1 on the highest elevation tone. Worst case here is 5.05:1. Do not 'correct' it back.

textDisabled.$description: Exempt from the 4.5:1 floor for the same stated reason as its light counterpart.

textInverse.$description: Ink on a saturated fill, and on the brand.

focus.$description: In dark the brand IS legible as a foreground -- 9.59:1 on surface -- so focus and primary are one colour here and two in light. That asymmetry is the palette doing its job.

primary.$description: Unchanged across themes. A yellow this saturated needs no night variant.

primaryHover.$description: Lighter in dark where light goes darker. Same rule -- toward the far end of the ramp -- opposite direction.

primarySoft.$description: A deep amber-navy, not a tint of the yellow: an alpha wash of #FACC15 over #1F2937 goes muddy at the opacity legibility needs.

primaryBorder.$description: Equal to the fill, so in dark there is effectively no border -- the fill already has 9.59:1 against surface and needs none. A colour rather than a null, so the light-to-dark lerp has no alpha discontinuity.

successDefault.$description: The brief's anchor, verbatim, in the theme it was chosen against. 7.79:1 with textInverse.

warningDefault.$description: Orange, for the same reason as its light counterpart. 7.84:1.

dangerDefault.$description: The brief's anchor. 4.71:1 with textInverse -- clear, with little room to spare, which is the empirical proof that a {semantic}.default must never be used as text.

infoDefault.$description: Was #3B82F6, the brief's anchor, until that turned out to be the shared channel palette's blue slot to the byte: a blue channel dot beside an info state read as the same thing. One step up keeps the hue and lifts contrast -- 6.98:1 under textInverse, 5.77:1 on the lowest surface.

channel.$description: The six named communication channels, shared by every preset -- WhatsApp is green whichever accent the app is wearing. Each is a {default, soft} pair per theme, because no single hex clears 3:1 on both a near-white and a near-black surface: a brand's identity is a hue, and contrast is a luminance, so the hue carries across and each theme stores the step of it that survives its own surface. Every pair is checked against BOTH presets' surfaces. No channel wears the brand yellow: a channel painted in the accent reads as a selected state. Channel *instances* -- a merchant's third WhatsApp number -- take an auto colour from the backend's own CHANNEL_COLOR_PALETTE instead, which mobile mirrors and never redefines.

whatsapp.$description: WhatsApp's own dark-green brand step, not a computed darkening of #25D366 -- which is 1.75:1 on white. 4.81:1 on its wash.

sms.$description: SMS has no brand. Violet is assigned to be distinguishable from the other five and from infoDefault, which is the only requirement a brandless channel has.

email.$description: Red, as the reference draws it. Email has no brand of its own -- the colour belongs to the medium.

instagram.$description: Instagram's identity is a gradient; the magenta stop is the only single value that survives being one 16px glyph, and the brief forbids decorative gradients.

liveChat.$description: Charcoal, as the reference draws it. It was yellow in an earlier draft; our own channel wearing our own accent is exactly the ambiguity the rule above forbids.

whatsapp.$description: The real brand green, which needs no adjustment on navy: 8.94:1.

liveChat.$description: Charcoal in daylight, its light counterpart at night. Never the accent.

type.$description: Fourteen steps, tuned for Arabic. Two properties are set on every step and both are decisions. lineHeight is a UNITLESS MULTIPLIER, mapping 1:1 onto Flutter's TextStyle.height and surviving text scaling -- authoring an absolute line height couples it to the size and breaks the moment one changes without the other. letterSpacing is 0 EVERYWHERE: Arabic is cursive, and Flutter's letterSpacing inserts advance width between glyph clusters, which severs the joins -- negative tracking on display type, a standard Latin move, is destructive here. The field exists because a future Latin-only step (a numeric readout) could use it, and it is zero on every step that can carry Arabic, which is every step. Heights are more generous than a Latin scale would use: the script has deep descenders and diacritics above the line. Weights are 400/500/700 only -- Tajawal has no 600, and a w600 request silently resolves upward to 700.

bodyLg.$description: Message text. The most generous leading in the scale, because this is where long Arabic paragraphs land.

labelLg.$description: Button and control labels. Tighter than body: a label is one line by design, so it does not need paragraph leading.

caption.$description: Timestamps and metadata. The one step with no Material slot -- reachable only as context.type.caption.

space.$description: Authored in rem at a 16px root, matching the web file's convention; the generator emits logical pixels. Named by size rather than by multiple, so a component asks for the step it means instead of counting.

radius.$description: Round numbers, and no derivation. The previous scale derived every step from a single base of 0.7rem and produced 7.2, 9.2, 11.2 and 15.2 -- values nobody chose, tracking a web variable mobile no longer shares. Controls land on sm/md, cards and sheets on lg/xl, and nothing is rounded to the point of reading as a consumer toy.

motion.$description: Subtle and functional. A component never reads these directly -- it reads context.motion, which returns a zeroed set when the OS asks for reduced motion, so no component checks a flag.

durationFast.$description: A press, a ripple, a checkbox.

durationNormal.$description: A theme crossfade, a banner, a state change.

durationSlow.$description: A sheet, a drawer, a page.

easingStandard.$description: Everything that is not an entrance.

easingEmphasized.$description: Entrances and anything that should feel like it arrived rather than appeared. Preserved from the previous theme -- it is the one motion value worth carrying across the re-theme.

pressScale.$description: What a pressable drops to while held. Collapses to 1 under reduced motion.
